name: TV Repair

pf.license.need: A business registration; where the state's rules require an electronic repair dealer registration, the business says its number (its own word) before it goes live.
ask: the business registration (the business's own word)
the electronic repair dealer registration number, where the state's rules require one (the business's own word)
a manufacturer's service authorization, only for warranty work the business says it does
liability insurance for in-home work, as the business says
pf.license.check: None: Rosie doesn't look up or check any registration, authorization or insurance (D96). The business says what it holds.
pf.license.blocks: A required registration the business says it doesn't hold keeps the work off; warranty work stays off until the business says it holds the manufacturer's authorization.
pf.license.renewals: The business's own record of renewal dates. A lapse the owner reports stops the work it covers.
pf.license.limits: low-voltage work only: a new power outlet behind a TV, or any in-wall power wiring, is an electrician's job and is never booked; mounting on brick, stone or above a fireplace only where the owner turns it on
pf.license.otherwise: identity: the code the customer gets on their own phone (D66); customers see no license claim

pf.services.shape: repairs of TVs, sound systems, receivers, game consoles and projectors: carried in to the shop (dropped off, checked, priced, fixed, picked up) or, for big TVs, fixed in the home; TV wall mounting in the home
pf.services.examples: the example shop's own prices, not a standard

list.name: TV, receiver or projector repair at the shop (carry-in)
list.price: a $65 bench check (example), counted toward the repair; the repair priced after the check
list.length: 3 to 7 days; a part on order can add 1 to 2 weeks
list.before: the $65 bench check paid when booking, as a deposit
list.after: the rest paid at the counter at pick-up

list.name: Game console HDMI port replacement
list.after: paid at the counter at pick-up

list.name: In-home TV repair (TVs 55 inches and bigger)
list.price: a $99 trip and check (example), counted toward the repair; the repair priced in the home
list.length: 1 to 2 hours; a part on order means a second visit
list.after: the saved card charged at DONE

list.name: TV wall mounting
list.price: $149 up to 65 inches, $199 bigger (example); hiding the cables in a low-voltage wall kit +$99
list.after: the saved card charged at DONE
list.note: two techs for TVs over 65 inches

list.name: Warranty repair (the manufacturer or a protection plan pays)
list.price: nothing for Alex when the plan covers it; anything it doesn't cover is quoted first
list.where: at the customer's home (big TVs) or the shop
list.after: the plan is billed; Alex gets a bill only for what it doesn't cover

pf.services.capacity: bench check-ins a day at the shop (8 at the example shop); one tech per home visit, two for TVs over 65 inches
pf.services.nobody_home: no: an adult is home for every home visit

beforeTimes: at the shop or at your home
what it is (a TV, a sound bar, a receiver, a game console, a projector)
what's wrong (no power, no picture, lines, no sound, a broken screen)
under a warranty or a protection plan?
for mounting: the screen size, the wall (drywall, brick, plaster), your mount or ours
afterTime: the model number (a photo of the label on the back helps)
where the TV is and any stairs
securePage: the warranty or plan's claim number
a device passcode, only if the repair needs it to test, and never in a text
pf.questions.whoMayBook: an adult: the owner of the device or someone they authorize

stop_words: smoke, sparks, flames or a burning smell from a TV or device
a battery that is swollen, hot, hissing or leaking (a remote, a controller, a sound bar)
a TV that fell, or someone hurt under a TV or stand
water or a drink spilled into a plugged-in device
an old tube TV opened at the back
pf.safety.stop_action: flames, smoke that won't stop, someone hurt or a shock: call 911 (Rosie never places the call); otherwise unplug at the wall only with dry hands and if it's safe, don't switch it back on, keep away from a swollen battery and never charge or puncture it, never open the back of an old tube TV (it can hold a deadly charge even unplugged)
pf.safety.continue: yes, after the safety steps, when nobody is hurt and nothing is burning: a repair visit or a drop-off

pf.first_steps.name: Repair authorization
pf.first_steps.when: signed on the secure page before the drop-off or the home visit
pf.first_steps.what: the bench or trip check fee, that no repair starts without the customer's yes to the price, that the customer backs up their data, and the shop's rule for devices not picked up

pf.first_steps.name: Prep
pf.first_steps.what: bring the remote and the power cord (carry-in); back up and sign out of accounts; for mounting, the wall clear and the TV out of its box

pf.visit.checkin: carry-in: the code at the counter and a claim tag; home: the code at the door
pf.visit.changes: the price is set after the check and the work waits for the customer's yes; a part found needed is priced first; a part on order means a second visit (home) or a later READY (shop); not worth fixing: only the check fee is paid and the device goes back or is recycled on the customer's yes
pf.visit.done: home: tested and working in front of the customer, DONE with a photo; shop: tested on the bench, READY, then picked up with the code

pf.money.main: carry-in: the bench check paid when booking and counted toward the repair, the rest at pick-up; home: a card saved, the trip check and the repair charged at DONE
pf.money.fees: A no-show or late-cancel fee inside 24 hours: none for carry-in (the bench check is the deposit); for a home visit, the trip and check ($99) is the visit's fee, the same as its late fee (one fee per booking); wall mounting $50. The owner's own numbers: the example shop's.
pf.money.extras: parts and extra work priced and OK'd by the customer before they're done
pf.money.warranty: a plan that pays is billed by the business; the customer pays only what it doesn't cover
pf.money.tax: sales tax on parts where the state's rules tax them (a generic switch)
pf.money.two: $2 per confirmed booking applies (D97): a flat fee for each booking Rosie makes.

skills: warranty work for the brands the business is authorized for
pf.staff.supervision: a new tech mounts with a senior tech until the owner OKs them
pf.staff.okWhat: the owner OKs any repair quote over $400
pf.staff.twoPeople: mounting a TV over 65 inches needs two techs: offered only when two are free
pf.staff.standin: another tech with the same skill may stand in; a customer who named a tech is never moved on silence

switches: a written estimate before the repair and the customer's OK before going over it, where the state's rules require it
replaced parts given back on request, where the state's rules require it
the notice before a device left unclaimed may be sold or recycled, by the state's rules
an electronic repair dealer registration number shown, where required
pf.rules.records: the work order, the estimate and the customer's yes kept with the booking

apply: a TV damaged at the visit
a warranty that doesn't cover the problem
pf.edges.handling: the generic way; the not-picked-up rule is the shop's own, by the state's rules

story.B: A tech comes to fix Alex's 75-inch TV at home: the $99 trip and check is promised, the repair is priced in the home, and the saved card is charged at DONE.

more: A short list of the few rules businesses like this usually set, ranked by the plug-in. Each row shows only where it applies.
Words: 'Businesses like yours often set these. Your call.' Never 'the law requires'.
Sam keeps them, unticks one, or taps one to change it. Each kept one becomes Sam's own rule.
Rows cover hours, cancel and any fee, same-day and new customers, and price OKs.
A fee row shows only where a card, a deposit or the full price is taken. It sets one late-cancel and no-show fee per booking.
When money was paid now, the fee is never more than what was paid now.
A fee is asked of Sam each time, never charged on silence.
For sensitive work, the suggested fee is $0: no fee unless Sam sets one.
Price OKs: quotes and bills over an amount come to the owner first. List prices never need an OK.
Sam's OK rules for requests are read at booking (A4-98 and B4-115). They cover same day, new customers, some services or dates.
A STOP before the pro sets out: the pro calls first. No answer in 15 minutes: the pro sets out.
Phone line: missed and after-hours calls go to Rosie's voice assistant. Every call opens with S13-01's words.
A call summary comes by text. A call only a person can take goes to a put-through number, never the owner's own mobile.
The phone-line row asks once for it: a staff phone or a second line that doesn't forward to Rosie.
Default: none, so the caller gets a callback. One that comes back to Rosie counts as nobody picked up (S13-56).
Kept on, the forwarding card needs one 'Done'. Later: the voice line stays off until it's done.
Bills Rosie sends: a tip line, and bank transfer over an amount, each only where bills are sent.
Where the plug-in allows it, a membership or a repeat plan charged monthly through Rosfield costs 1% of each charge.
It pays no $2 on its visits or members' classes.
A member who pays elsewhere: Rosie can't see it.
So each class they book is $2 at check-in, where the plug-in allows it.
So one row asks: take bookings from members who pay elsewhere? On unless Sam turns it off. Off: those bookings are declined (A4-80).
Not shown, kept at a safe default: the owner's text hours, 8am to 8pm, with same-day requests anytime.
Also months offered, peak dates, terms by customer, reasons with no fee, signed dated schedules and who may book.
Also the waitlist, one bill for many visits and the no-show count, all off. Stand-ins are offered, never on silence.
Each is on the summary (S1-79). Sam changes any by text or a call, or in the portal (S11-56).
Only the business's own customers may book: a row only where the plug-in suggests it. Else Sam sets it by text or a call.
Deposit or fee caps the plug-in knows show as suggested rows. They're the owner's own rules, never Rosie's checks.
Sam's answer clock runs only in Sam's text hours. Same-day requests reach Sam anytime.
Where Sam's OK rules cover it, like a new customer, Sam gets 5 minutes, any hour. Silence sends nobody (B4-115).
A booking keeps the rules it was made with. Every text's arrival and free-cancel times come from these settings.
For a drafted plug-in, the suggestions come from the closest known kinds and the checklist, reviewed with the draft.
Never: charge a fee on silence, or let a suggestion run before the owner keeps it.
Safe default: every suggestion kept as shown, any fee asked each time.
ops.why: The sent-now branch is off here, so the sign-up card's sent-now lines go (addendum self-check 1).
